newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey extends deadline in fresh water tender.
newsitem.headline: Turkey extends deadline in fresh water tender.

text.p: Turkey extended the deadline in a tender for a project to lease a fresh water purification and treatment plant for sales to thirsty Middle Eastern countries, the Official Gazette said on Friday.
It said the deadline was extended to March 31 from the original date of February 14.
It did not give any reason why the entension was made but officials said Turkey's state hydraulics authority (DSI) had received no bids.
The project will cost the winner $100 million, according to the tender terms.
The operator will first complete unfinished construction work, started in 1992 by the government but halted due to financial problems.
It will later operate the plant, located on the Manavgat river in the south, and market fresh water, to be produced at a daily rate of 500,000 cubic metres.
The operator will also build a 10-km (six-mile) twin pipeline to carry water from the plant to a loading port.

The project is part of the government's revenue raising packages and expected to bring in 120 trillion lira over its entire lease life of 20 years. The government will get royalties from the operator.
Officials has earlier said Israel, Libya, Malta and Italy were expected to show interest in the project.
They say per tonne production cost of Manavgat water will be up to $3, compared to $6 in water produced through seawater desalination, a method used by several Middle East countries.
Some output of the plant is also planned for Turkey's southern tourist resorts like Kemer, Belek and Bodrum.
